newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt to brief Israel's Levy on Syria talks - TV.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to brief Israel's Levy on Syria talks - TV.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy will go to Cairo on Thursday to be briefed on President Hosni Mubarak's recent talks with Syrian President Hafez al-Assad, Israeli television stations said.
Israel's Channel One and Channel Two television stations said Levy was invited to Egypt by Foreign Minister Amr Moussa, who wanted to update Levy on Mubarak's talks in Damascus on Monday.
The Foreign Ministry spokesman was not immediately available to comment.

Assad told a joint news conference with Mubarak on Monday that he did not rule out an Israeli attack on Syria or Lebanon. Levy and other Israeli officials swiftly reacted, saying Israel had no intention of attacking Syria.
Mubarak said at the news conference that recent Syrian military exercises, which have spurred war jitters in Israel, should not be taken as preparation for war.

Israel and Syria have held sporadic peace talks since October 1991. The negotiations have deadlocked over the fate of the Golan Heights captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war. Syria demands return of the strategic plateau.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he will not give up the Golan. The previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May elections, was ready to make at least a partial withdrawal for full peace with Syria.
